title: Prevent updates of disabled inputs in `AppTest`
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [x] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It would be great, if `AppTest` would check whether an element is disabled before updating its value. Trying to do so should lead to an error or at least a warning.

### Why?

When running AppTests I sometimes stumble upon cases, where the tests work even when they shouldn't ... just for me to find out, that again I changed values of disabled elements within the tests and `AppTest` happily does that.

Having at least a warning would make it easier to find those quirks in the tests.

### How?

Nothing needs to change in the interface.

For convenience and backward compatibility it would be possible to include a flag in `AppTest` to configure the behavior, e.g. `at = AppTest('test_main.py', default_timeout=30, on_update_disabled_element='warning')`
with the possible values:
- `accept`: take the new value without complaint (default, current behavior)
- `warning`: take the new value and issue a warning
- `error`: raise an error when trying to update a disabled element

### Additional Context

Below you can find a short example to illustrate the problem: currently the test succeeds even though changing the value would not be possible in the app itself.

To run the example
- save the code as `test_main.py`
- run `pytest`

```python
import streamlit as st
from streamlit.testing.v1 import AppTest

st.text_input('Text', value='initial value', disabled=True, key='k_text')


def test_disabled_input():
    at = AppTest('test_main.py', default_timeout=30)
    at.run()

    at.text_input(key='k_text').set_value('new value')
    at.run()

    assert at.text_input(key='k_text').value == 'new value'
```

[USER] I tested this again with recent versions. It seems to be fixed starting with 1.61.0, probably due to #16209. At least the widget does no longer accept the new value if it is disabled.

For debugging purposes I think it would be beneficial to issue a warning or error, when an AppTest tries to update a disabled element. Right now the behavior is:
- `ignore`: simply drop / ignore the new value
